sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface labeling with anti-HA antibody confirmed extracellular display; the construct was used for surface expression studies in transfected cells. Quantitative functional data (e.g., current amplitude, voltage dependence) for the tagged channel vs. untagged are not reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: L4 explicitly names the junction as between G284 and I285 with a 7-aa linker and states the tag is extracellular. The canonical 889-aa sequence has K at positions 284-285 (intracellular, 264-289); a Python search for GI in extracellular spans finds exactly one match at canonical positions 311-312 (ECL2, 309-324), consistent with a 27-residue N-terminal offset between the paper's isoform and the canonical sequence. The junction at 311 is 3 residues from the TM3 C-terminal boundary (308) and 13 residues from the TM4 N-terminal boundary (325), satisfying the ≥3-residue rule. ECL2 contains no cysteines and no NxS/T glycosylation sequons. PMC6894927 reports full-length HCN2 (in pEGFP-C1) with an HA-tag inserted between residues the paper calls G284 and I285 via a 7-aa linker (ISAYGIT-YPYDVPDYA), described as extracellular. The paper uses a shorter isoform/mouse-HCN2 numbering that is 27 residues shorter at the N-terminus than the canonical 889-aa human sequence; the only GI motif in an extracellular region of the canonical sequence is at positions 311-312 (ECL2, 309-324), confirming the junction is our G311-I312. Python search confirmed: seq[310]='G', seq[311]='I', offset=311-284=27.

sources.claim: The HA-tag sequence is inserted between amino acids G284 and I285 by means of a 7aa long linker (linker-HA-tag: ISAYGIT-YPYDVPDYA).

literature_notes: L3 (PMC6894927) is the same paper as L4 and provides only the general statement that HCN2 contains an 'extracellular HA-tag sequence'; L4 from the same paper pins the junction to G284-I285 and supersedes L3 as the residue-level evidence. L1 and L2 (PMC10717812) report a C-terminal FLAG tag on HCN2 used for surface biotinylation assays; the C-terminus (position 889) falls entirely within the intracellular domain (461-889) and therefore does not qualify as a surface tag site — it is recorded in other_positions. The confidence for the ECL2 site is 'medium' rather than 'high' because the residue assignment required resolving a 27-aa isoform numbering offset; the paper's explicit statement that the tag is extracellular and the unique GI match in ECL2 make the assignment robust, but the offset is inferred rather than stated by the authors.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on HCN2 used for surface biotinylation; the C-terminus (889) is in the intracellular domain (461-889) and is not accessible from the extracellular face.
